question: Should consecutive malformed paired-node audio payloads intentionally count toward the existing five-error cutoff that stops the Google Meet audio bridge?
rationale: The code is internally consistent and well-proven, but applying the transient-input cutoff to a newly recognized validation failure changes the bridge's availability behavior and requires owner intent.

options.title: Use the existing cutoff
options.body: Treat malformed payloads like other repeated node input failures and stop the bridge after five consecutive errors.

options.title: Drop without stopping
options.body: Reject and warn on malformed payloads without advancing the bridge-stop counter, keeping the bridge alive during persistent malformed input.

recommendation.title: Use the existing cutoff
recommendation.body: Treat malformed payloads like other repeated node input failures and stop the bridge after five consecutive errors.

likelyOwner.reason: The related feature history attributes the existing paired-node failure cutoff to this contributor's merged Google Meet reliability work.
